The landlord asked us to let the contractor in with the office key without the tenants, which I refused because it needs consent or 24h written notice. I messaged the landlord, tenants and provider, and put the job on hold until 16 Oct.

args.body: Hi Freya, thanks for your message. We can't let the contractor in with the spare key without the tenants' agreement. Holding a key doesn't give us a right of entry, and entering without consent or proper notice isn't something we can do. The lawful route is written notice to the tenants of the visit, at least 24 hours ahead. We are doing that now and still trying to reach them. The contractor has told us they are aiming for Monday 20th PM, but we are confirming that date and which company is attending. We'll update you by Wednesday 16 October.

tickets.description:
The toilet is running slow to fill up and the cold water tap in the hand basin in the bathroom isn't working at all this has become a issue recently on our return from our holiday.

Additional details provided:
- Is this the only toilet at the property? Yes
- Is the toilet not flushing, blocked and overflowing, constantly running or trickling, or something else? Trickling to fill up
- When you flush, does the water drain away at all, or does it rise up toward the rim of the bowl? Drains away
- Are there any access considerations we should know about, such as entry codes or alarms and security systems that would need to be disarmed? No
- Are there any pets at the property? Yes
